text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents a non-review research study focused on assessing spatial uncertainties in future land use allocation across Europe (EU27), which constitutes an explicit national-scale spatial implementation across multiple countries. The primary objective is to evaluate how uncertainties in macro-level assumptions (GDP and population) within two contrasting future scenarios—Marketeer and Musketeer—affect the spatial allocation of agricultural land (arable and pasture), making LULC prediction/simulation central to the research question. The study implements two quantitative future scenarios with explicit comparison of their outcomes, uses the Dyna-CLUE spatial land use model to generate 1×1 km gridded projections of land use change (including abandonment and expansion), and reports quantitative metrics such as probabilities of land use occurrence, standard deviations, confidence intervals, and significance thresholds (e.g., ≥95% consistency across 50 model runs). Outputs include mapped projections of LULC transitions at both grid and administrative levels. The study meets all core inclusion criteria and does not trigger any exclusion criteria—it is not global-only, not local/regional only, includes LULC prediction as a core focus, provides spatially explicit outputs, uses multiple scenarios, and reports quantitative accuracy/uncertainty metrics.)
